name: Zagora
hero_subtitle: Gateway to the Sahara: palm-lined Draa Valley, the famous Timbuktu sign, nearby dunes and the quiet rhythm of southern oasis towns.

overview.title: Welcome to Zagora — palms, caravan memory and the road to the dunes
overview.p1: Zagora sits in the Draa Valley of southern Morocco, long a staging post on routes that once ran toward Timbuktu. Today the town is quieter than the big imperial cities, framed by expansive date-palm oases and the Anti-Atlas mountains. This historic desert market town offers the unique atmosphere of a Saharan gateway.
overview.p2: Most travellers stop for the iconic “Timbuktu 52 days” sign, a walk or drive through the palm groves, a short outing to the Tinfou dunes, and a half-day in Tamegroute for green pottery and the historic library. Amezrou and Jebel Zagora add village lanes and a sunset climb.
overview.p3: Two to four days is enough if you want oasis time plus one desert night. Summer is extremely hot; the classic season runs from autumn through spring when evenings cool and the light on the palms is soft.

places.title: Must-visit places in Zagora
places.subtitle: Palm valley, desert edge, pottery village and the caravan sign.

draa_valley.title: Draa Valley Palm Groves
draa_valley.desc: A river of date palms and earthen villages — the green heart of the road to Zagora.

timbuktu_sign.title: Timbuktu 52 Days Sign
timbuktu_sign.desc: The most photographed sign in the south — a reminder of the old camel caravan route.

tinfou.title: Tinfou Dunes
tinfou.desc: Accessible sand dunes south of town — a first taste of the Sahara without a long expedition.

tamegroute.title: Tamegroute
tamegroute.desc: Green pottery workshops and a historic Koranic library about 20 km south of Zagora.

amezrou.title: Amezrou
amezrou.desc: Earthen lanes and the old Jewish quarter — a walkable heritage corner of the oasis.

jebel_zagora.title: Jebel Zagora
jebel_zagora.desc: The mountain above town — climb early for palm-grove and desert-edge views.

souk_zagora.title: Zagora Souk
souk_zagora.desc: A working regional market for dates, produce and everyday Draa Valley life.

desert_camps.title: Desert Camps & Camel Treks
desert_camps.desc: Overnight camps and camel rides toward the dunes — the classic Zagora desert experience.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-day plan for Zagora
itinerary.subtitle: Oasis and sign first, then Tamegroute or dunes, then a desert night or free day.

day1.title: Town, sign & palms
day1.desc: Timbuktu sign, palm-grove walk and sunset toward Jebel Zagora.

day2.title: Tamegroute or Tinfou
day2.desc: Pottery and library in Tamegroute, or an afternoon on the Tinfou dunes.

day3.title: Desert or Amezrou
day3.desc: Camel trek and camp, or a slower village morning in Amezrou before departure.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Photo stop at the famous sign, then orient yourself in the centre.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Walk or drive through Draa Valley palms and earthen villages.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Climb or viewpoint for sunset over the oasis if energy allows.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Green pottery workshops and the historic library south of town.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Short dune outing if you want sand before a desert night tomorrow.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Simple oasis meal and early night if a camp is booked.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Start a trek toward camp, or explore Amezrou lanes at a slow pace.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Dune time and tea, or packing and a last palm-grove walk.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Desert night sky, or return to town for onward travel.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: Town is compact; Tamegroute, Tinfou and desert camps need a taxi, tour or rental. Agree prices before long desert tracks.

bargain.title: Heat & water
bargain.desc: Summer is extreme. Carry more water than you think you need, high SPF and a hat. Prefer early starts for Jebel Zagora and dunes.

water.title: Cash & season
water.desc: Carry dirhams for taxis, guides and small stops. Book desert camps ahead in peak winter season.

q1.question: How many days in Zagora?
q1.answer: Two days cover the sign, palms and Tamegroute or Tinfou. Three to four days suit a desert night plus a slower oasis pace.

q2.question: Is Zagora only a stop to the desert?
q2.answer: Desert camps are a big draw, but the Draa palms, Tamegroute, Amezrou and Jebel Zagora make the oasis itself worth time.

q3.question: How do I get to Zagora?
q3.answer: Most visitors come by road from Ouarzazate (about 2.5–3 hours) or on longer routes from Marrakech via the south.

q4.question: Best time to visit?
q4.answer: October to April for milder days. Summer heat can exceed 45–50°C and limits outdoor plans.
